extracted.intended_audience: ICLR 2024 reviewers (peer reviewers for an ML conference)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for reviewers assessing submissions to ICLR (machine-learning conference), including what to read for, how to structure reviews, ethical reporting, discussion participation, and final recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and substantive reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Your reviews are timely and substantive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meet the stated deadlines for bidding and review submission; provide sufficiently detailed, thoughtful reviews (not brief or perfunctory). Top reviewers are acknowledged; main reviewer tasks/dates are provided (create/update profile, bid, write review, discuss, provide recommendations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to the Code of Ethics (CoE)
rubrics_metrics.description: All reviewers must read and adhere to the ICLR Code of Ethics; raise potential CoE violations as part of the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting your review, complete the CoE report form (asks whether there's a potential violation and, if yes, to explain). Flag potential CoE violations for AC/PC/ethics board to handle. Authors may include an ethics discussion section (not counted against page limit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Carefully read the paper (and related work)
rubrics_metrics.description: It’s important to carefully read through the entire paper, and to look up any related work and citations that will help you comprehensively evaluate it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give yourself sufficient time. Consider objective, strong/weak points, and look at supplementary material when helpful. Be mindful of biases and be open-minded about a paper's value to the broader ICLR community.

rubrics_metrics.name: What is the specific question and/or problem tackled by the paper?
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the precise research question or problem the submission addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the goal is applied, conceptual, theoretical, or a combination; different objectives require different considerations for value and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the approach well motivated and well-placed in the literature?
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the submission provides clear motivation for the approach and situates it appropriately among prior work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check literature placement and justification of novelty/relations to prior methods; use judgement for comparisons to very recent work (see contemporaneous policy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the paper support its claims (correctness, rigor, reproducibility)?
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine if results (theoretical or empirical) are correct and scientifically rigorous, and whether evidence supports the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect proofs/derivations and assumptions, experimental design, statistical significance, reproducibility details (hyperparameters, seeds, number of runs), and whether supplementary material clarifies missing details.

rubrics_metrics.name: What is the significance of the work?
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the contribution's importance: does it bring new knowledge and sufficient value to the ICLR community?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significance need not be state-of-the-art performance; work can be impactful through novel insights (empirical, theoretical, or practical). Evaluate relevance and potential impact for the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarize what the paper claims to contribute
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a concise, positive summary of the paper's claimed contributions in your review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be constructive; begin the review with a clear restatement of claims to show understanding and orient readers/ACs.

rubrics_metrics.name: List strong and weak points comprehensively
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerate the submission's strengths and weaknesses in detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be as comprehensive as possible. Include technical, empirical, and presentation strengths/weaknesses to justify the recommendation and to give useful feedback to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: State a clear initial recommendation (accept or reject) with reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly state your initial recommendation and provide one or two key reasons for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the decision explicit (accept/reject/leaning); succinctly justify the recommendation with the most important supporting reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide supporting arguments for your recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Back up your recommendation with detailed evidence and reasoning drawn from the paper and related literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point to specific experiments, theoretical results, or missing elements that drive your decision; explain trade-offs where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask questions for the authors (to clarify or elicit additional evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pose specific questions you want authors to answer in the discussion/author response phase to resolve uncertainties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions should clarify assumptions, experimental settings, derivations, baselines, or other gaps that affect your assessment; use them to guide authors toward providing the evidence you need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide constructive feedback to improve the paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer additional feedback aimed at helping the authors improve their work (may be independent of the accept/reject decision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame comments as helpful suggestions, not merely criticisms; separate improvement suggestions from decision-critical points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete the CoE report when submitting your review
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit the short CoE report form alongside your review: indicate whether there is a potential ethics/code-of-conduct violation and explain if so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the Code of Ethics before reviewing so you can answer the form accurately; report concerns confidentially when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage actively in the discussion phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Participate in asynchronous discussions with authors and other reviewers and be open to changing your initial recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-examine your assessment in light of author responses and other reviewers' comments; be willing to move score up or down based on new evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend and prepare for borderline-paper meetings when requested
rubrics_metrics.description: For borderline cases, reviewers may be asked to join virtual meetings organized by ACs; reviewers should familiarize themselves with other feedback beforehand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These meetings are scheduled only for borderline papers; reviewers who fail to attend (absent emergencies) may have their input weighed accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a final recommendation after discussion and revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Update your review after the discussion phase and any paper revisions, stating your final recommendation and what changed (or didn't).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document reasoning for any change in recommendation and reference new evidence from discussions or revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for additional experiments should be limited in scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may ask for additional experiments, but they should not request experiments that significantly change the submission's content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested experiments should be limited and intended to more thoroughly validate existing results rather than extend the paper's scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of supplementary material
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary material is optional to read but can often answer questions raised while reading the main paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult supplementary material before asking authors questions, as it may contain necessary details for reproducibility or clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling arXiv and contemporaneous work / expectations about comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are recommended to ignore arXiv-only versions and use judgement when expecting authors to compare to very recent work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers published within four months prior to the submission deadline are considered contemporaneous; authors are not required to compare to such very recent peer-reviewed work, and may be excused for not knowing about arXiv-only papers. Reviewers should use their judgment and consult AC if in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid bias and be open-minded about broader community value
rubrics_metrics.description: Be mindful of potential biases and try to be open-minded about the value and interest a paper can have for the entire ICLR community, even if not personally appealing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate a paper's potential impact beyond your own immediate interests; explicitly consider whether personal taste or domain preference is influencing your assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical correctness and experimental rigor (detailed checks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess theory and experiments for correctness and rigor: clarity of assumptions/proofs, correctness of derivations, experimental details, tuning, baselines, and statistical significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From examples: check novelty claims (are theorems novel?), assumptions about function classes, validity of proofs/derivations, clarity of algorithms and equations, whether experiments report sufficient details (policy, reward settings, architectures, hyperparameter tuning, number of runs), whether statistical significance is shown, and whether baselines are appropriate and fairly tuned. Note specific common reviewer complaints in examples (missing details, unclear derivations, improper comparisons).
